requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen: Today (22) and All (135) at the top, then My Lists, each with a coloured icon and its open count. Counts update after adding and deleting.

Open tasks come first, then a 'Completed (n)' section header with a chevron that collapses and expands it. Tapping the circle completes a task (red filled check, strikethrough) or reopens it, and the task returns to its original position.

Add sheet (title, notes, list, priority) and the edit sheet opened by tapping a row both work; title, notes and priority edits save. But turning on the Due Date switch freezes the app every time (2 of 2 tries, in both the New Task and Edit Task sheets). The switch stops mid-animation and nothing responds again until the app is killed, so a due date can never be set.
Overdue dates show in red with a red '!' badge and 'Overdue'. High priority shows a red '!!!' and low priority a grey '!'. Today groups tasks under an 'Overdue' header.

Swipe to delete is the native trailing Delete action and the delete persists. Reorder is hidden behind ⋯ > Reorder Tasks, which shows grab handles, but dragging a handle (tried at 3 speeds) never moved a row.
Add List alert creates a list (empty state: 'No Tasks'). ⋯ > Rename List… and Delete List… (with a confirmation alert) both work.
After relaunch the added task, the completed and reopened task, the edit, the deletion and the renamed or deleted lists all persisted.

bugs: Turning on the Due Date switch in New Task or Edit Task freezes the whole app: the switch stops mid-animation, Cancel and every other control stop responding, and the app has to be killed (the unsaved task is lost). Reproduced every time.
Dragging the reorder handles in Reorder Tasks mode never moves a row, so tasks cannot be reordered.
An empty list shows 'All tasks are completed.' above the 'No Tasks' empty state, which contradict each other.
tells: Reordering needs a trip into the ⋯ menu ('Reorder Tasks') instead of the usual Edit mode or drag-to-reorder.
The disclosure chevrons are exposed to accessibility as disabled buttons named 'chevron'.
A.scroll: The 180-task All list (grouped by list, with coloured section headers) scrolls smoothly when dragged slowly, flung and flung back. No blank or popping rows; content passes under the bar with the system blur, and the large title collapses correctly.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen with Today (22), All (135) and My Lists with counts; counts update after changes. Every list has the same orange icon.
Open tasks first, then 'Completed (n)' with a Show/Hide text button; collapsed by default. Tapping the circle completes a task (blue check, greyed out) or reopens it.

Adding works: title, notes, a due-date switch with the native compact calendar picker, priority segments and a list picker. But tapping any task to edit it crashes the app straight to the Home Screen (3 of 3 tries, from a list and from All), so editing is impossible.
Overdue dates show in red with an 'Overdue ·' prefix; high priority shows a red '!!!'. Low priority is not marked.
Each row's always-visible grip reorders by dragging, and the new order persists. Swiping left shows a Delete action that works.
+ opens a New List alert; the ⋯ menu has Rename List and Delete List (with a confirmation alert); all of them work.
The new task, the deletion, the reorder, the renamed list and the deleted list all survived a relaunch.

bugs: Tapping any task row (to edit it) crashes the app immediately. Reproduced from a list and from All, every time.
On Today, the ⋯ menu disappears and only + is shown, which is inconsistent with the list screens (minor).
tells: Reorder grips (≡) are shown on every row all the time; iOS shows them only in Edit mode.
The swipe action is drawn by hand: a small floating red trash pill with a 'Delete' caption under it, not the full-height system swipe button. The row's separator also disappears while it is open.
Every list has the same orange icon, so lists cannot be told apart by colour.
The task list is a plain white list with a separator line above the first row, and the last open row's separator runs edge to edge. It does not look like a standard plain or inset List.
The Completed section uses a 'Show'/'Hide' text button where a disclosure chevron is expected.
All is one flat, unsorted list mixing tasks from every list, with no section per list.
In the compact date picker, the selected day is a black circle instead of the accent colour.
B.scroll: Lists scroll smoothly when dragged slowly, flung and flung back to the top. No blank rows or popping, and the large title collapses normally.

why: Each app has one showstopper in requirement 3: A freezes when you set a due date, and B crashes whenever you tap a task to edit it. B's crash is worse because tapping a row is the most common thing a user does, and it leaves no way to edit anything. A is also the more convincing iPhone app: colour-coded inset-grouped lists, system swipe actions, a disclosure-style Completed section and lists grouped by section in All. B has always-on grips, a hand-drawn swipe button and identical orange list icons. B's working drag-to-reorder doesn't make up for that.
